steps.say: Six in ten liver lumps in children are malignant. The embryonic liver cancer takes four fifths of the malignant share and one percent of all childhood cancer, peaking at three years, while the adult-type liver cancer strikes older children around ten to eleven years.
steps.tx: Paediatric liver tumours are malignant in **60** (sixty) percent, **hepatoblastoma** (embryonic liver cancer) takes **80** (eighty) percent of malignant cases and **1** (one) percent of paediatric cancer with **peak incidence** (commonest age) at **3** (three) years, while **hepatocellular carcinoma** (adult-type liver cancer) strikes older children at a median **10** (ten) to **11.2** (eleven point two) years.

steps.say: Family syndromes and chronic liver injury set the stage. Bowel polyp syndromes and overgrowth disorders raise the embryonic cancer, while hepatitis viruses, metabolic liver diseases and long-standing bile blockage raise the adult-type cancer. The history therefore reviews bowels, growth charts and liver disease, hunting clues.
steps.tx: **Familial adenomatous polyposis** (bowel-polyp syndrome), Gardner and **Beckwith Wiedemann** (overgrowth disorder) raise hepatoblastoma risk, while **hepatitis B** (liver virus) and C, **tyrosinemia** (metabolic disease), **glycogen storage disease type 1** (sugar-store defect), **alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency** (protein defect) and **biliary atresia** (blocked ducts) cholestasis raise carcinoma risk.

steps.say: A painless swelling in the upper belly with weight loss and anaemia leads, jaundice comes late, a burst tumour bleeds into the abdomen, and a quarter have already spread to nodes, lungs, marrow or brain. The liver map shows where each tumour family lives, guiding the cut.
steps.tx: A painless **abdominal mass** (belly swelling) with anorexia, weight loss and **anemia** (pale blood) leads, jaundice stays rare until with **tumour rupture** (burst bleed) bleeding into the peritoneum, and a quarter (**25** (twenty five) percent) show **metastatic spread** (distant deposits) to nodes, lung, marrow and brain. The tumour-location map places hepatoblastoma, **HCC** (adult-type cancer) and bile-duct cancers in their **segments** (liver zones).

vis.caption: Tumour locations across the liver and biliary tree. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The blood marker rises in seven of ten cases but also climbs in germ cell tumours and in benign liver lumps of small babies, so it never stands alone. Sound waves trace the vessels, cross-sectional scans define anatomy, hepatitis testing is mandatory, and the chest is scanned for lung spread.
steps.tx: **Alpha fetoprotein** (liver-tumour protein) rises in over **70** (seventy) percent but also rises in **sarcoma** (connective-tissue cancer), **yolk sac tumour** (germ-cell cancer) and **hamartoma** (benign lump) under **6** (six) months, all carcinoma suspects need **hepatitis testing** (virus screen), and **Doppler ultrasound** (flow-tracing scan) maps vessels before **computed tomography** (detailed scan) defines anatomy with chest CT hunting lung spread.

steps.say: The surgical map divides the liver into four sections by tumour-free neighbours, from one section involved to all four. Early stages with free sections come out by removing a segment or lobe, while advanced disease shrinks first with drugs. Vascular invasion and spread outside the liver change the plan.
steps.tx: **PRETEXT** (surgical liver map) divides the liver in **4** (four) sections by tumour free neighbours from I one involved to IV all involved, adding caudate, **rupture** (burst), ascites, focality, **nodes** (glands), **metastases** (spread) and **vascular invasion** (vessel entry). Stages I and II take **upfront resection** (immediate removal) by **segmentectomy** (section removal) or **lobectomy** (lobe removal).

steps.say: Drug therapy centres on platinum with supporting agents, pure early fetal-pattern disease skips drugs entirely, and transplant rules cap the tumour count and size without spread beyond the liver or into vessels. The transplant drawing shows the native organ coming out and the donor organ going in.
steps.tx: Standard drugs are **cisplatin** (platinum drug), **5 fluorouracil** (antimetabolite) and **vincristine** (vinca drug) with **doxorubicin** (red drug), **irinotecan** (topoisomerase drug) and **ifosfamide** (alkylator) for relapse, pure fetal stage I skips **chemotherapy** (drug treatment), and **transplant** (organ replacement) criteria cap at three tumours under **3** (three) cm without extrahepatic or vascular disease. Advanced disease shrinks first with **neoadjuvant chemotherapy** (pre-surgery drugs) before resection or transplant.

vis.alt: Surgical diagram of orthotopic liver transplantation with native removal and donor placement.
vis.caption: Native liver out, donor organ in: the transplant rescue. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Resectable disease now cures the large majority, matching transplant results for disease that cannot be cut out. The adult-type cancer relapses after partial removal and earns early transplant consideration. High-risk flags are very high marker levels, spread beyond the liver, distant deposits, burst tumours and vessel invasion. Transplant listing starts at diagnosis for disease that cannot be cut out.
steps.tx: Resectable **hepatoblastoma** (cuttable embryonic cancer) exceeds **85** (eighty five) to **90** (ninety) percent **disease free survival** (cure rate) matching transplant results for **unresectable tumour** (uncuttable disease), while carcinoma relapses after partial **hepatectomy** (liver removal) and earns early transplant consideration. Transplant listing begins at diagnosis for **unresectable** (uncuttable) disease to avoid losing the window.

steps.say: A marker above one hundred, disease outside the liver, distant deposits, bleeding into the abdomen and tumour in the great veins or the portal trunk all warn of trouble. These children need the most intensive drugs and the earliest transplant discussion.
steps.tx: High risk flags are **alpha fetoprotein** (tumour protein) above **100** (one hundred), spread beyond liver, distant **metastases** (spread deposits), **intraperitoneal bleed** (belly bleeding) and **hepatic vein** (liver-vein), caval or portal invasion. Such cases take intensified **chemotherapy** (strong drugs) with early **transplant evaluation** (replacement workup).
